learningObjective: Describe what typically goes into a model deployment package (weights + graph + metadata) and why the packaging boundary matters for reproducibility.

canonicalClaims.claim: A production model package contains graph structure, weights with metadata, IO signatures, and pre/post-processing metadata, versioned by an archive schema; each component is required for correct deployment and reproducibility.
conditions: Deployment must be reproducible, portable and possibly offline.
The runtime must be able to load and execute the model without additional out-of-band information.
nonImplications: Does not imply a single-file format is mandatory; multi-file bundles are common in the LLM community.
Does not imply preprocessing must be in the compiled artifact; it may live in a companion config.

misconceptions.claim: Only the weight tensors need to be shipped.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Graph structure and signatures are needed; runtimes cannot infer them from weights alone.

misconceptions.claim: Weights can be random-initialized at deployment.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Random weights produce random outputs; trained weights are required.

misconceptions.claim: Downloading model artifacts on every start is standard practice.
misconceptions.whyWrong: This couples deployment to network availability and hurts reproducibility.

misconceptions.claim: Pre/post-processing metadata is unnecessary because the runtime handles it.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Tokenizers, normalizers, and calibration scales are model-specific and must be shipped.
